item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Suggestions to continue in another Copilot experience
item.description:
Updated November 13, 2026: We have updated the Rollout schedule to reflect timing for Standard and Deferred audiences.

[What and why]

The Chat experience in the Copilot app will suggest a better-fit mode based on the user's prompt, if applicable. For example, it will suggest Cowork or other supported modes as they become available. Users will see a suggestion card after they send a prompt in Chat, with an explanation of the better-fit mode and an option for the user to switch to the suggested mode. Their chat conversation will be attached to the prompt in the new mode to maintain context. Only users who have the Copilot mode (example Cowork) enabled will see this experience.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Standard (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026
  • Deferred (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-December 2026 and expected to complete by late December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who have access to supported Copilot modes, such as Cowork.

Platforms and services

  •  Microsoft Copilot

What will happen

  • After sending a prompt in Chat, if Copilot determines that another Copilot experience available to the user may better fit a request or task, the user may see a banner suggesting that experience.
  • In the banner, the user will see an option to switch to the suggested experience (ie. Cowork) or remain in Chat. 
  • If the user selects the option to switch, they will be brought directly to the suggested experience with the prompt already sent, along with the context from their Chat conversation attached.
  • Users will see suggestions only for experiences they can access. For example, users who do not have access to Cowork will not see a suggestion to use Cowork.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required to prepare for this change.

Consider informing your users and help desk that Copilot may suggest another Copilot mode when that mode may better fit a request or task.

Consider reviewing which users are included in a spending policy that grants Cowork access, and confirm your intended usage-based billing configuration. 

[Compliance considerations]

 No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint: Generate smart tables of contents for PDFs on the web with Copilot
item.description:
Updated November 13, 2026: We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time. We apologize for any inconvenience. 

[What and Why:]

We are introducing Smart Table of Contents (Smart TOC) in the Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint PDF viewer on the web for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. When a PDF does not already contain a table of contents, users can ask Copilot to generate a hierarchical, clickable structure that makes it easier to navigate long documents and move between sections. This feature is available only on the web in the initial release and is generated only when a user explicitly requests it.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCCH, DoD): We have decided not to move forward with this change at this time.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

  • Who is affected: Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license who access PDF files in OneDrive and SharePoint on the web.
  • Platforms/Services: OneDrive, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 Copilot, PDF viewer on the web.

What will happen:

  • The Smart TOC entry point will appear when an eligible user opens a PDF that does not already contain table-of-contents information.
  • The feature is available only in the OneDrive and SharePoint PDF viewer on the web during the initial release.
  • Mobile and desktop applications are not included at this time.
  • Copilot analyzes document structure and generates nested, clickable entries mapped to pages or page ranges.
  • Users with edit permissions can save the generated table of contents into the PDF.
  • The saved table of contents can be displayed by compatible PDF editors.
  • Users with view-only permissions can generate and use Smart TOC for navigation but cannot save the generated table of contents.
  • Smart TOC is available only to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • AI-generated content may be inaccurate, particularly for scanned or OCR-based PDF files.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No immediate admin action is required.

Before rollout, you may want to:

  • Review Microsoft 365 Copilot license assignments for users who should have access to this capability.
  • Inform eligible users, helpdesk personnel, and support teams about the new PDF navigation experience.
  • Update internal documentation to clarify that saving a generated table of contents requires edit permissions on the PDF.
  • Encourage users to validate AI-generated table-of-contents entries when accuracy is important.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed? Yes. Copilot processes PDF content that the licensed user is already authorized to access in order to generate a table of contents for navigation. Existing file permissions are respected, and saving changes requires edit permissions.
  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? Yes. Copilot analyzes PDF document structure and generates an AI-created hierarchical table of contents. The experience is user-initiated and does not run automatically.
  • Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Yes. Eligible users can request Copilot to generate a table of contents for PDF files that do not already contain one.
  • Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves? Yes. The feature is user-initiated and only runs when a licensed user chooses to generate a Smart TOC.

The experience will clearly indicate that the table of contents was AI generated and may contain inaccuracies.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] Microsoft Entra ID: Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for SMS and voice multi-factor authentication
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Entra ID is adding safeguards to protect telephony-based multifactor authentication (MFA) from automated fraudulent activity. Some users who use SMS or voice for MFA may be asked to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends an SMS verification code or initiates a verification call.

This change is separate from the planned retirement of SMS and voice authentication and does not affect the retirement timeline.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide: Beginning in mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use SMS or voice for Microsoft Entra ID multifactor authentication

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • SMS and voice authentication methods

What will happen

  • Some users may be prompted to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends an SMS verification code or initiates a verification call.
  • The verification step will appear only for authentication attempts that meet sufficiently high-risk thresholds.
  • Users with restrictive network or firewall settings may be unable to complete SMS or voice MFA if the verification experience cannot load.

[Action required and recommendations]

We recommend that administrators take the following actions:

  • Prepare your help desk and notify users that some SMS and voice MFA attempts may require an additional CAPTCHA verification step.
  • Review the risk-based anti-bot verification documentation for network-readiness guidance. If your organization uses restrictive firewalls, proxies, or web filtering, ensure that the required resources can load during authentication.
  • Continue moving users to phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, where possible.

Learn more

  • Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for telephony-based sign-in - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Understanding telephony fraud risk for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform - Information regarding the end of support for SharePoint temporary authentication URLs
item.description:
Starting April 1, 2027, SharePoint temporary authentication URLs will be retired. Power Apps and Automate functionality that relies on these URLs will break when they are retired.

How does this affect me?
Any Power Apps app or Power Automate cloud flow that relies upon the temporary authentication URLs will stop working.

What action do I need to take?
If you are using only native controls, actions, and connectors, and as long as you are not providing pre-authenticated URLs from SharePoint, then there is no action needed.

If you have authored a custom control, action, or connector with tempauth URLs, then you will need to ensure you have migrated to the new authentication. This may come up in a few ways such as:
  • SharePoint document-library thumbnails not loading
  • SharePoint-stored Images displayed through Image control not loading
  • For the Word Online (Business) connector, CreateWordFileWithContent currently returns a pre-authorized URL that can be used to download the generated document without additional authentication. After temporary authentication is removed, customers should no longer rely on this URL as an unauthenticated file-download mechanism.
After making the required changes, publish updated apps or save and publish updated flows, as applicable. Ensure the updated apps and flows are enabled and tested before the retirement date

For more information on this, visit Pre-authenticated (tempauth) URLs are retiring: move to Microsoft Entra ID tokens before April 1, 2027.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Facilitator proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps in meetings
item.description:
Updated November 12, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why]

We are introducing a new Microsoft Teams Facilitator capability that proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps during meetings. Facilitator can identify when participants ask questions or express uncertainty and retrieve and share relevant answers using web search in the meeting chat. This enhancement helps improve meeting productivity by reducing interruptions and enabling teams to stay focused on goals while accessing needed information. If a participant asks a factual question and no one responds, Facilitator can provide an answer directly in the meeting chat.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558341.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning early February 2027 (previously early December) and expected to complete mid-February 2027 (previously mid-December)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-February 2027 (previously mid-December) and expected to complete early March 2027 (previously mid-January)

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Users in Microsoft Teams meetings where Facilitator is enabled with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams (meetings)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Facilitator will monitor meeting conversations in real time to detect implicit or explicit information needs.
  • When a knowledge gap is identified, Facilitator performs a web search and posts a response in the meeting chat: 
  • Responses are infrequent in practice and typically occur less than once per meeting.
  • Responses are limited to questions relevant to the meeting discussion based on agenda signals and conversational context.
  • Facilitator must be manually added to the meeting and is not enabled by default.
  • A user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license must enable Facilitator for the meeting. Other participants do not need to be licensed to receive responses.
  • Admins can disable Facilitator at the tenant level. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting. If web search is disabled, responses are not generated.
  • Users can stop the behavior at any time by removing Facilitator from the meeting.
  • The feature is supported in standard Teams meetings only and not supported in calls, webinars, or town halls.
  • The experience is supported in meetings that include external or cross-tenant participants.

[Action Required/Recommendations]

No immediate action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review your organization’s Copilot web search and Facilitator configuration settings to confirm alignment with your policies.
  • Inform helpdesk and users about proactive Facilitator responses in meeting chats.
  • Update internal documentation or training materials if you reference Teams meeting experiences.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (for example, meeting conversations)?Yes. The feature processes meeting conversations in real time to detect knowledge gaps and generate responses.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Facilitator uses AI to interpret meeting content and generate contextual responses during meetings.
Does the change provide end users with a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users receive proactive, AI-generated responses within the Teams meeting chat without needing to prompt the system.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through configuration settings?Yes. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting, which admins can enable or disable to control functionality.
Does the change allow a user to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. Users can stop the behavior by removing Facilitator from the meeting.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilot Workspaces is replacing standalone agent selection with agentic chat
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft 365 Copilot Workspaces (formerly Copilot Notebooks) is moving to an agentic chat experience. As part of this change, Researcher, Analyst, and Designer will no longer be available as standalone agent options within Copilot Workspaces.

Instead of selecting or switching between agents, users can describe what they need in plain language. Copilot will automatically apply the appropriate research, analysis, or design skills based on the request and the workspace content.

This change simplifies the user experience while preserving existing capabilities. Researcher, Analyst, and Designer will remain available as separate agents in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app for users who prefer working with a specific agent.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Frontier preview: Rollout is planned to begin in December 2026. The completion date has not yet been determined.
  • Rollout dates for general availability are still being finalized. We will provide additional information when available.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of Microsoft 365 Copilot Workspaces who have access to the Frontier preview

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Workspaces (formerly Copilot Notebooks)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot app

What will happen

  • Standalone agent selection: Researcher, Analyst, and Designer will no longer appear as separate agent options within Copilot Workspaces.
  • Agentic chat: Users can describe research, analysis, and design tasks in natural language. Copilot will automatically apply the appropriate skills based on the request and workspace content.
  • No loss of capabilities: Research, analysis, and design capabilities will remain available within Copilot Workspaces.
  • Simplified workflow: Users will no longer need to select or switch between agents when performing different tasks.
  • Continued access to individual agents: Researcher, Analyst, and Designer will remain available as separate agents in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • Default behavior: This change will apply automatically when it rolls out to your organization.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Inform users that Researcher, Analyst, and Designer will no longer appear as separate agent options in Copilot Workspaces.
  • Explain that users can describe their tasks directly in chat, and Copilot will apply the appropriate capabilities.
  • Update internal training and support materials that instruct users to select specific agents within Copilot Workspaces.
  • Direct users who prefer working with individual agents to Researcher, Analyst, and Designer in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • Monitor Message center for additional rollout information.

[Compliance considerations]

This change introduces an agentic chat experience in Copilot Workspaces, allowing users to interact with research, analysis, and design capabilities through natural language rather than selecting individual agents.

Organizations should review this change as appropriate for their compliance requirements.

item.title: [planForChange] Scheduled prompts in Microsoft 365 Copilot are moving to native Copilot scheduling and the Tasks view
item.description:
[What and why]

We are updating scheduled prompts in Microsoft 365 Copilot to use native Copilot scheduling infrastructure instead of Power Platform. Users can continue scheduling one-time or recurring tasks using natural language, with Copilot executing tasks automatically and returning results to the associated conversation. The new experience operates independently of Power Platform, including where Power Automate is disabled, and processes and stores scheduled task data within the Microsoft 365 compliance boundary.

The existing Power Platform-based scheduled prompts experience will retire on December 31, 2026.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Frontier/TAP: November 11, 2026
  • Worldwide rollout: November 30 through December 31, 2026
  • Retirement of Power Platform-based scheduled prompts: December 31, 2026

Rollout timing may change based on reliability and migration readiness.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot premium license who use scheduled tasks, subject to organizational controls

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat
  • Tasks in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app
  • Web and Windows desktop

What will happen

  • Users can schedule one-time or recurring tasks that Copilot executes automatically, even when users are not present.
  • Users can run, edit, pause, resume, or delete scheduled tasks, with limits of 10 active and 50 total schedules per user: 

  • Tasks requiring user approval will pause until the user responds in the associated conversation.
  • Users will manage Copilot Chat schedules from Tasks > Scheduled in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • For 30 days after the Scheduled tab becomes available to a user, scheduled tasks will be accessible from both the existing shared-header More options (...) menu and Tasks > Scheduled. After this period, the existing menu entry will be removed.
  • Responses from previously completed scheduled runs will remain available.
  • Power Platform-based scheduled prompts will retire on December 31, 2026.

[Action required and recommendations]

We recommend that administrators:

  • Notify users who rely on scheduled prompts about the transition.
  • Advise affected users to recreate schedules that will not migrate automatically before December 31, 2026.
  • Inform users that management of Copilot Chat scheduled tasks is moving to Tasks > Scheduled.
  • Update internal documentation and helpdesk guidance.
  • Review applicable Microsoft 365 Copilot controls and organizational policies.

No action is required to preserve responses from completed scheduled runs.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Scheduled tasks will execute through native Microsoft 365 Copilot scheduling infrastructure instead of the existing Power Platform-based scheduling path. Scheduled task data will be processed and stored within the Microsoft 365 compliance boundary.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Copilot can execute one-time or recurring scheduled tasks without requiring users to be present and return results to the associated conversation.
Does the change provide end users with a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can delegate future or recurring tasks to Copilot for automatic execution at a specified time or frequency.
Does the change allow users to enable and disable the feature themselves?Yes. Users can pause, resume, edit, manually run, or delete individual scheduled tasks, subject to applicable organizational controls.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Windows: Updates to address compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
item.description:
Updated November 11, 2026: On November 16, 2026, an update will be released for Microsoft Edge and WebView2, delivered via the PKI Metadata component, which will fully remove default trust for the remaining roots (emSign Root CA - G1, emSign Root CA - C1, emSign ECC Root CA, and emSign Root TLS CA - G1). Devices check for PKI Metadata updates every 10 hours and shortly after each new app launch. 

For more information, see Microsoft Response to eMudhra Certificate Authority Key Compromise.

[What and why]

Microsoft is responding to an issue involving eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) private keys, six associated with TLS and two with code signing. Because these keys could be recovered, they could potentially be used to create certificates or sign content that appeared to come from a trusted CA. The issue arose in eMudhra's certificate hierarchy and was not a compromise of Microsoft systems.

Microsoft is updating certificate trust to block affected certificate authorities and remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Windows, Microsoft Edge, or WebView2, particularly organizations with certificates that chain to one of the eight certificates being removed
  • Organizations managing disconnected Windows devices or disconnected Azure devices may need to take additional action

Platforms and services

  • Windows
  • Microsoft Edge
  • WebView2
  • Azure virtual machines

What will happen

  • Microsoft has published an update to the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List to block the affected certificate authorities.
  • Microsoft has deployed a separate CRLSet update for Microsoft Edge and WebView2 to block affected TLS certificates signed by the affected certificate authorities.
  • The Microsoft Edge and WebView2 update is delivered automatically through the component update mechanism. Customers do not need to install a new browser version.
  • Microsoft has released updates to Windows and Microsoft Edge to remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies from their trust lists.
  • After these updates reach a device, the affected certificates will no longer be trusted by default through the respective trust lists.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Keep updates flowing. Allow automatic Windows certificate trust updates and Microsoft Edge component updates to reach your devices.
  • Check disconnected Windows devices. If you manage Windows devices that do not receive automatic updates, make sure your update process delivers the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and upcoming trust-list changes. See the Microsoft Learn guidance in Learn more for information about distributing certificate trust lists in disconnected environments.
  • Review disconnected Azure devices. Review disconnected Azure devices running on Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) or single-instance VMs. Updated images are available in Azure Marketplace, and customers can deploy them to protect against this vulnerability.
  • Replace dependent certificates. If any of your certificates chain to one of the seven certificates being removed, identify those dependencies and obtain replacement certificates or an alternative trusted chain before the changes reach your devices.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Malicious QR code detection in messages
item.description:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is extending malicious URL protection to provide near-real-time detection of malicious destinations embedded in QR codes shared in messages. Teams will analyze QR code destinations to identify potential phishing and fraud threats and display an additional warning when malicious content is detected.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use Microsoft Teams messaging

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams chats, meeting chats, and channels

What will happen

  • Teams will decode and evaluate QR code destinations in inline images shared in 1:1 chats, group chats, meeting chats, and channels.
  • Detection applies to internal and external communications.
  • Images containing QR codes from external senders are already blurred by default. When Teams identifies a malicious QR code, users will also see the warning, “This message contains a link that might be harmful,” and a “Learn about file and link safety” link.
  • QR code images from internal senders are not blurred by default. The same warning will appear when Teams detects a malicious QR code.
  • For users on Teams mobile in China, QR code images are blurred by default regardless of whether the sender is internal or external, and any messages containing malicious QR code will be blocked.
  • Malicious QR code detection is managed by the existing Malicious URL protection setting.
  • The setting is enabled by default. Organizations with Malicious URL protection enabled will automatically receive malicious QR code detection as the feature rolls out.
  • No separate configuration is available or required for malicious QR code detection.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Admins can review or change the existing Malicious URL protection setting in Teams admin center > Settings and policies > Messaging Safety.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users and help desk staff about the additional warning for detected malicious QR codes.
  • Clarify that QR code blurring is a separate precautionary experience and does not mean that Teams has identified a QR code as malicious.
  • Review internal documentation about Teams messaging security and update it if necessary.

item.title: [planForChange] Discover usage-based billing (UBB) experiences like Cowork, Code, and Autopilot
item.description:
[What and why:]

As previously announced in MC1479277, we are making usage-based experiences in the Microsoft Copilot app easier to discover. Usage-based billing experiences like Cowork, Code, and Autopilot, will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, even if their organization has not enabled access. Users without an applicable spending policy will see an option to request access or learn more, based on their organization's settings.

Based on customer feedback, we are extending the rollout timeline and introducing an additional admin control that will allow organizations to provide custom guidance to users. These changes give administrators more time to prepare and greater flexibility to manage how users discover and request access to usage-based experiences.

[Rollout schedule:]

The updated rollout schedule is as follows:

  • Mid-November 2026: The new admin setting, "Access requests to usage-based billing experiences," will become available for administrators to configure.
  • Mid-December 2026: An additional option will be introduced to the admin setting, allowing administrators to provide a custom URL as part of the Learn more informational experience that directs users to their own organization’s guidance. The option will be available if you select "Specific users" or “No users” in the setting.
  • End of January 2027: The new discoverability behavior and admin setting will be enforced. The old setting "Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing" will be retired. This will apply to customers on deferred release at the end of February 2027.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: 

  • Organizations with users licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Platforms/services: 

  • Microsoft Copilot app and Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • Entry points for Cowork, Code, and Autopilot will be visible by default to licensed users starting at the end of January 2027.
  • Users without an applicable spending policy giving them access to the feature will see an informational experience with an option to "Request access" or "Learn more," depending on their how their organization has configured the new "Access requests to usage-based billing experiences" admin setting.
  • Administrators can configure which users are eligible to request access, including the option to prevent access requests.
  • Administrators will be able to provide a custom URL directing users to organizational guidance. Only users who cannot request access will see the secondary URL, "Your organization’s guidance", as part of the Learn more informational experience.  
  • The existing setting, "Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing," will continue to apply until it is retired at the end of January 2027.

Examples of the customizable “Your organization’s guidance” link on the informational experience for Cowork and Code. UI subject to change.

This change does not automatically enable usage-based experiences or initiate billing. Users must have an applicable spending policy and available Copilot Credits before they can use these experiences.

[Action required / recommendations:]

We recommend that administrators:

  1. Review the new setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings > Access requests to usage-based billing experiences when it becomes available in mid-November. Starting mid-December, you will be able to configure a custom URL in this setting for users who you decide cannot request access.
  2. Configure access request preferences to determine which users can request access to usage-based experiences.
  3. Prepare organizational guidance and, beginning in mid-December, configure a custom URL if you want to direct users to information specific to your organization.
  4. Review spending policies to ensure that access to usage-based experiences aligns with your organization's requirements.

We recommend reviewing and configuring these settings before the new discoverability behavior is enforced at the end of January 2027.

Learn more: Access requests to usage-based billing experiences (This will be updated in mid-Dec to reflect instructions for the custom URL once available in the setting)

[Compliance considerations:]

This update introduces additional administrative controls for managing access requests and organizational guidance. It does not automatically grant users access to usage-based experiences or change existing spending policy requirements.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Simplifying AI access: Introducing usage-based billing
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the rollout scope and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

The new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business combines everyday AI through a user subscription license with Advanced AI through usage-based billing. Beginning in mid-November, 2026, usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made by new tenants. This phased approach makes it easier for new customers to access eligible usage-based AI experiences, including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities, while reducing billing complexity and preserving flexibility to expand usage over time based on business needs. 

This change will not apply to your existing Microsoft 365 tenant as part of the November rollout. We will share additional information before making usage-based billing easier to enable for existing tenants. If you’d like to get started sooner, you can enable usage-based billing at any time through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

What is changing 

  • Eligible purchases made by new tenants: Beginning in mid-November, pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business and Microsoft 365 Business with Copilot purchases made by new tenants. 
  • If the new tenant does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and spending policy, they will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup. 
  • The resulting spending policy will have a spending limit of 4,000 Copilot credits per user per month, with charges based on actual usage. 
  • Charges apply only when these experiences are used, subject to the usage controls and spending limits established by the administrator. 
  • We will begin rolling out this change to eligible customers in supported markets. The change will not initially be available in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Italy, Korea, the Netherlands, Poland, or Spain. We plan to include these markets in the next phase of the rollout in early 2027, with additional details and timing to be shared closer to launch. 

What is not changing 

  • Your existing Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscription benefits and payment terms do not change.
  • Usage-based billing will not be configured by default for your existing tenant as part of the November rollout. 
  • If your organization already has a spending policy configured, the existing spending policy remains in place. 

When this will happen 

  • Mid-November 2026: Usage-based billing default-on will begin for eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made by new tenants directly from Microsoft, including through Microsoft web. 
  • Existing tenants: We plan to make usage-based billing easier to enable for existing tenants across all markets beginning in early 2027. We’ll share more details, including specific timing and what to expect, closer to launch. 
  • Optional action: Existing tenants can turn on usage-based billing at any time through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  • Starting in early 2027: The change applies to eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made through Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) channels, with specific timing to be shared closer to launch. 

How usage-based billing works 

  • When usage-based billing is configured, the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and spending policy support access to eligible usage-based experiences. 
  • If you want to turn on usage-based billing for your existing tenant, you can create and manage a spending policy through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  • Your organization can adjust its spending policies and controls to align with its needs. Disabling usage-based billing prevents access to experiences that require it. 

What you can do to prepare 

  • Review which eligible usage-based experiences—including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities—may support your organization’s needs. 
  • Review your organization’s usage-based billing, governance, and cost-management requirements. 
  • If you choose to turn on usage-based billing ahead of this update, you can create or adjust usage controls and spending policies in Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

Learn more 

  • Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center: https://admin.cloud.microsoft/#/copilot/costmanagement/overview 
  • Usage-based billing and cost management for Copilot Credits: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits 
  • Cloud Based Billing: What is a cloud subscription? - Microsoft Cost Management | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing support for Microsoft Agent 365 agents that implement the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, allowing them to be used as connected agents in declarative agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Began in late August 2026 and is expected to complete by end of December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 administrators who manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Developers building declarative agents with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Users who are assigned access to approved Microsoft Agent 365 agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

What will happen

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action may be required.

Before rollout:

  • Review Microsoft Agent 365 agents available in the All agents page of the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Determine which Agent2Agent-enabled agents should be made available to users in your organization.
  • Review connected agents associated with declarative agents from the Connected agents tab before approving their use.
  • Update any internal governance, agent approval, or deployment processes as appropriate.

Consider notifying administrators and developers in your organization about the availability of Agent2Agent-connected agents and the associated review and approval process.

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance considerationAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. This update introduces support for Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents within declarative agents. Organizations should review how these connected agents interact with customer data before approving them for use.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with declarative agents that are connected to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling new AI-powered experiences and workflows.
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can install, review, and approve Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents through the Microsoft 365 admin center before they are available for use.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot Feedback UX update
item.description:

[What and Why:]

We’re updating the thumbs-down feedback experience in Microsoft Copilot to make it easier for users to provide specific, actionable feedback. Today, many thumbs-down responses are submitted without comments, providing sentiment but limited information about the issue. When users select thumbs down, they’ll be able to select one or more feedback categories and optionally provide additional comments, giving each categorized response a signal that can be routed to the appropriate team or issue type.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late October).

Users who can submit feedback in supported Microsoft Copilot experiences may see the updated thumbs-down feedback form. The planned audience includes users signed in with Microsoft Entra ID organizational accounts, users signed in with consumer Microsoft accounts, and users in Education tenants. The feature isn’t currently planned for Mobile, GCC, GCC High, DoD, or other sovereign cloud environments.

The updated feedback experience is planned for Microsoft Copilot, Copilot in Microsoft Edge, Copilot in Microsoft Outlook, and Copilot in Microsoft Teams, across web browsers, Windows, and macOS. The WXPN/Catalyst experience isn’t currently included.

When a user selects thumbs down on a Copilot response, they may see selectable categories describing the issue, can select more than one category, and can optionally enter additional feedback in a free-text field. The thumbs-up feedback experience isn’t changing. This update applies only to the existing “Allow users to submit feedback to Microsoft” admin policy; all other feedback policy experiences remain unchanged. During the controlled rollout, some users will continue to see the existing feedback experience.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required for this change. It will be visible to users who are already allowed to submit feedback under the existing policy.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer

Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. This UX change applies to the existing "Allow users to submit feedback to Microsoft" admin policy; all other feedback policy experiences remain unchanged.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Gov rollout of this feature is still paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by late November 2026 (previously early November) via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and November 23, 2026 (previously November 3) for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only. For organizations running on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online in a Hybrid Deployment, migrate to Dedicated Hybrid App. For organizations hosted in Exchange Online sharing with another organization running Exchange on-premises, kindly monitor future Message Center posts for guidance on migration paths as they become available. 

[Additional information:]

  • Migration guide: Migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy for sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips.
  • Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy Microsoft Graph API Overview
  • Exchange Online EWS, Your Time is Almost Up

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint: Annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs on the web
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint on the web will support annotation for PDFs encrypted with Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels. Users who have the appropriate editing usage rights will be able to annotate protected PDFs in their browser without removing the sensitivity label. The file's sensitivity label, encryption, and usage rights will be preserved when changes are saved.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late January 2027 and expected to complete in late January 2027

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • OneDrive for Business and SharePoint customers
  • This feature does not apply to OneDrive Consumer.

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web
  • All browsers are supported.

What will happen

  • Users who have editing usage rights can annotate sensitivity label-protected, encrypted PDFs in the OneDrive or SharePoint web PDF viewer.
  • Available annotation tools include ink, highlight, free text, notes, signatures, image/shape/date stamps, bookmarks, and form fields.
  • Users can save annotations without removing the sensitivity label.
  • The sensitivity label, encryption, and usage rights are preserved when the annotated PDF is saved.
  • Users with view-only rights will continue to see the PDF as read-only and cannot annotate.
  • This change does not grant users additional access or editing rights.
  • No feature-specific admin control or configuration is required. Existing sensitivity label and usage-rights settings determine who can view or edit protected PDFs.

[Action required and recommendations]

No feature-specific admin action is required to enable this update.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users who routinely review labeled or regulated documents that they can annotate protected PDFs in place.
  • Confirm that your sensitivity label and usage-rights configuration reflects who should be able to edit or view protected PDFs.
  • Update internal documentation and helpdesk guidance as appropriate.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is accessed or modified?Yes. Users with existing editing usage rights gain a new way to modify protected PDFs by adding annotations in the OneDrive or SharePoint web PDF viewer.
Does the change preserve Information Protection label behavior?Yes. Users can annotate PDFs protected by sensitivity labels without removing the label. The sensitivity label, encryption, and usage rights are preserved when the file is saved.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Purview: Retirement of select DSPM partner integrations

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Changes to custom organizational data in MODS for Workforce Insights
item.description:
[What and why]

We're changing how the Workforce Insights agent receives custom organizational data from Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service (MODS). The separate Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS will be retired. Going forward, organizational data will reach the Workforce Insights agent through the Microsoft 365 profile endpoint. The Workforce Insights agent is part of the Microsoft Frontier program and is currently in preview.

Ingestion of custom public attributes through Microsoft 365 profile is already generally available. For custom non-public attributes, customers who currently use the Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS or wish to enable this capability for the first time, must join the private preview.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Workforce Insights endpoint retirement (Frontier preview) in MODS: Starting November 18, 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizational Data Source Administrators in organizations that send custom attributes to the Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS
  • Organizations that plan to use custom attributes in Copilot experiences and the Workforce Insights Agent
  • If your organization doesn't send custom attributes to the Workforce Insights endpoint today, no immediate action is required

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service
  • Microsoft 365 profile
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Workforce Insights agent

What will happen

  • After November 18, 2026, the Workforce Insights endpoint will no longer be available as a destination in MODS. To ingest custom public attributes, use the Microsoft 365 profile endpoint in MODS.
  • To bring custom non-public attributes (such as job level) into Copilot experiences and the Workforce Insights Agent, your organization must join the private preview.
  • Your current Workforce Insights endpoint selection won’t carry over. You must explicitly select the Microsoft 365 profile endpoint in MODS.
  • Data previously uploaded to the Workforce Insights endpoint will remain stale and continue to serve the Workforce Insights Agent and organizational queries in Copilot. You won't be able to upload subsequent data through the retired endpoint. See how to manage your data in MODS documentation in the Learn more section below.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization currently sends custom non-public attributes to the Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS, complete these actions before November 18, 2026:

  • Identify what attributes you ingest to Workforce Insights endpoint today. Ingest updated public attributes using Microsoft 365 profile endpoint in MODS. 
  • For non-public attributes, request to join the private preview by contacting wficomm@microsoft.com. Work with privacy and data governance stakeholders to determine the access policy and then ingest data to the Microsoft 365 profile endpoint. Keep in mind that these attributes will also be available to Copilot experiences as capabilities continue to roll out, not only the Workforce Insights Agent.
  • Don't select the Workforce Insights endpoint for new uploads, even if it's still available when your preview starts.
  • Complete the switch before November 18, 2026.

Learn more

  • Overview of Workforce Insights Agent
  • Introduction to Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service 
  • Import and manage your organizational data with a .csv file - Microsoft 365 Apps | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. For existing customers who has ingested custom attributes through Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS, the uploaded data will be made available to Microsoft 365 profile, Copilot experiences and Workforce Insights agent.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The change modifies how custom organizational attributes are made available to the Workforce Insights agent and Copilot experiences.

item.title: [planForChange] Copilot Cowork: Power Platform connectors now follow Microsoft 365 admin center settings
item.description:

Microsoft Copilot Cowork now supports Power Platform connectors published as plugins, with connector availability managed through the Microsoft 365 admin center. This enables organizations to extend Cowork to third-party applications and services while giving administrators centralized control over which supported connectors can be used. Cowork respects these settings when creating connections and executing actions, helping organizations extend AI-powered business processes with enterprise-level manageability.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

Organizations using Microsoft Copilot Cowork that want to use Power Platform connectors to connect Cowork with third-party applications and services.

Platforms/Services:

Microsoft Copilot Cowork, Power Platform connectors, and the Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • Administrators can allow or block supported Power Platform connectors through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Cowork respects these settings when creating connections and executing actions, including connections established before a connector was blocked.
  • Connector policies also apply to Cowork Automations.
  • Additional Power Platform connectors are being added to the Microsoft 365 admin center. Connectors become available in Cowork as they are added.
  • Existing Microsoft 365 capabilities for email, calendar, Teams, and files are unaffected.
  • Power Platform admin center Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies do not apply to Cowork.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Review available connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Tools.
  • Configure connector availability based on your organization's requirements.
  • Review your organization's governance requirements before enabling Power Platform connectors for Cowork, noting that Power Platform admin center DLP policies do not apply to Cowork.

[Compliance considerations:]

This change introduces Power Platform connector integrations between Copilot Cowork and supported third-party applications and services. Administrators can manage supported connector availability through the Microsoft 365 admin center. Power Platform admin center Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies do not apply to Cowork.
